config.title: Controlled Input

intro.title: Controlled Input
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple form with a text input field that displays its current value in real-time. You will learn the concept of a controlled input, where the React component state is the single source of truth for the input's value. The main technologies involved are React's useState hook and TypeScript for type-safe state management. By the end, you will understand how to synchronize form data with component state to create responsive and predictable user interfaces.
intro.usecase: Controlled inputs are the standard pattern for building interactive forms and data-entry interfaces in professional React applications. You'll use them to create responsive settings panels where user selections instantly update the UI, such as in dashboard filters that refine displayed charts or in modal forms for submitting user data. This approach ensures the React state is the single source of truth, which is critical for validation, dynamic feedback, and reliable data handling in features like search bars, configuration wizards, and admin consoles.

objectives: Initialize React state to store input values in TypeScript
Bind input elements to React state using controlled component patterns
Implement event handlers to update state when user input changes
Render input values dynamically from state in the component UI
Configure form elements to be fully controlled by React state
Manipulate multiple input fields with individual state management
Apply TypeScript interfaces to define and enforce input value types

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The imports are added at the top of the file, making React and useState available for use.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to import both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: import both React and useState from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Create the main component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named ControlledInput that returns a JSX element. You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax.
steps.hint:
Define a component that returns a simple JSX element like a
or

to start.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the ControlledInput component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named ControlledInput is defined and returns JSX.
successCriteria: The component is named ControlledInput and returns valid JSX (e.g., a <div> or other element).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component is named exactly 'ControlledInput' and returns JSX.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Check the name and that it returns JSX.

steps.title: Initialize state with TypeScript
steps.instruction: Inside your ControlledInput component, initialize a state variable called inputValue using useState. Type it as string and set its initial value to an empty string.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. The syntax is: const [inputValue, setInputValue] = useState<string>('')
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: state initialization with TypeScript
const [name, setName] = useState<string>('');
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable called inputValue that is typed as string and initialized to an empty string.
successCriteria: inputValue state is initialized with useState, typed as string, and set to empty string initial value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with string type annotation and empty string initial value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The state initialization is missing or incorrect. Remember to use useState<string>('') for the inputValue state.

steps.title: Define the change handler function
steps.instruction: Inside your ControlledInput component, define a function called handleChange that takes a React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement> parameter and updates the inputValue state with event.target.value.
steps.hint: The function should receive the event parameter and call setInputValue with the value from the event target.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a handleChange function that updates the inputValue state when called with an input change event.
successCriteria: A handleChange function is defined that takes a React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement> parameter and calls setInputValue with event.target.value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your handleChange function properly receives the event parameter and calls setInputValue with event.target.value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleChange function is missing or doesn't match the required structure. It should take a React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement> parameter and update the state with event.target.value.

steps.title: Add the input element structure
steps.instruction: In your ControlledInput component's return statement, add an <input> element.
steps.hint: The input element should be a JSX tag. It can be self-closing: <input />.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will now render a basic input element in the UI.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the input element structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added an <input> element inside the return statement.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input element is missing. Add an <input> element to the return statement.

steps.title: Connect input value to state
steps.instruction: Set the input element's value attribute to the inputValue state variable to make it a controlled input.
steps.hint: In JSX, you can set an input's value using the value attribute and bind it to your state variable.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: binding input value to state
<input value={someState} />
steps.expectedOutcome: The input element will display the current value from the inputValue state, making it a controlled input.
successCriteria: The input element has a value attribute set to the inputValue state variable.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've set the value attribute on the input element to the inputValue state variable.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input element should have a value attribute connected to the inputValue state variable. Try setting value={inputValue} on the input element.

steps.title: Wire the onChange event
steps.instruction: Set the onChange attribute of the input element to call the handleChange function when the input value changes.
steps.hint: Add the onChange prop to the input element and assign it the handleChange function reference.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: wiring an event handler
<input onChange={handleInputChange} />
steps.expectedOutcome: The input element will have an onChange handler that triggers when the user types, though the handler function body is still empty.
successCriteria: The input element includes an onChange attribute set to handleChange.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added the onChange attribute to the input element with the correct handler function name.
steps.feedbackWrong: The onChange event isn't properly wired. Check that you've added the onChange attribute to the input element.

steps.title: Display the current state value
steps.instruction: Add a paragraph element below the input that displays the current inputValue state.
steps.hint:
Place a

tag after the input element and use curly braces to embed the inputValue variable inside.
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying a state value in JSX

Current value: {someState}
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show the input's current value below the input field, updating in real-time as you type.
successCriteria: A paragraph element is added after the input that displays the current inputValue.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a paragraph, but it might not be displaying the inputValue correctly. Make sure to use curly braces to embed the state variable.
steps.feedbackWrong:
The paragraph element is missing or not displaying the inputValue. Add a

tag after the input with {inputValue} inside.

steps.title: Add a reset button with handler
steps.instruction: Add a button element after the paragraph that, when clicked, resets the input value to an empty string.
steps.hint: Create a button with an onClick handler that calls setInputValue with an empty string.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: button that resets a value
<button onClick={() => setCount(0)}>Reset</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will include a button that clears the input field when clicked.
successCriteria: A button element is added with an onClick handler that calls setInputValue('').
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it has an onClick handler that calls setInputValue('').
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or doesn't reset the input value correctly.
